content: In 2022, new recommendations were developed for the management of tuberculosis (TB) in children and adolescents, particularly in high TB burden settings. These recommendations suggest that decentralized TB services can be utilized for children and adolescents who exhibit signs and symptoms of TB or have been exposed to TB. This is a new conditional recommendation based on evidence with very low certainty. Additionally, family-centered and integrated services, alongside standard TB services, may also be employed for children and adolescents with signs and symptoms of TB or those exposed to TB. This is another new conditional recommendation, also supported by evidence with very low certainty. These recommendations are sourced from the World Health Organization (WHO) consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, specifically Module 5, which focuses on the management of TB in children and adolescents, published in 2022.
